newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani cotton rates end steady, seen falling.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani cotton rates end steady, seen falling.

text.p: Pakistani cotton rates closed unchanged on Tuesday as spinners bought selectively and dealers said prices could fall on increased supply.
The Karachi Cotton Association (KCA) said it had reversed an earlier decision to close the market today for a local holiday at the request of its members.
In the kerb market NIAB-78 variety of 1996/97 crop was traded at 2,400 rupees ($67.39) per maund (37.32 kg) while MNH-93 was traded at 2,450 rupees, dealers said.
"Supply is on the rise and rates will ease in the next few sessions," dealer Adil Naseem said.
